newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Century says mine talks progress slow.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Century says mine talks progress slow.

text.p: RTZ Plc-CRA Ltd unit Century Zinc said negotiations with local Aboriginal groups who are opposed to the A$1 billion Century zinc mine in north Queensland are continuing but in-depth talks have yet to start.
"I think it (the talks) is proceeding as fast as it can. We have had preliminary information sharing but no in-depth talks," Century's managing director Ian Williams told Reuters.
"The (state) government has to drive the process. It is our understanding that some further meetings will be held in the Gulf region with serious talks starting in about three weeks," Williams said.
The Queensland government has appointed former Australian governor-general Bill Hayden to negotiate with local Aboriginal groups under provisions of the Native Title Act.
The state, which had been preparing enabling legislation to deliver security of land tenure to Century, withdrew its own legislative programme in July at the request of RTZ-CRA.
Williams said preliminary discussions between Hayden and Aboriginal groups had identified a number of points needing clarification.
"One of the issues is to try and get a collective view from claimants who have different claims on the one piece of land," Williams said.
There were currently seven groups with Native Title claims including five over the mine site's lease area and the remainder over the proposed slurry pipeline, he said.
Negotiations are expected to last four months with a six-month arbitration process allowed if agreement is not reached by December 5.
Meanwhile, Century Zinc was continuing to liaise with various communities in the Gulf region surrounding the mine, Williams said.
"There is a huge interest out there for jobs," Williams said.
Century had set a target for Aboriginal workers to be 50 percent of the mine's workforce in the first two or three years of the project he said.
Century has warned that the longer the negotiating process takes, the less chance there is of supplying zinc from the project to the Netherlands Budel smelter.
Pasminco Ltd was to be Century's biggest customer, purchasing half the production of the low iron bearing zinc concentrates for Budel.
Century's development is crucial to continued operations of Budel whose current licence requires it to halt the production of jarosite, a zinc process residue, by June 1998.
